requirement: An annotation or outline item may carry an action to perform on activation; this is a trigger-site statement, not an obligation to implement every action subtype.
errata: No applicable EC3 correction found in doc/errata-read.md or the effective EC3 text.
evidence: Link annotations read /A through action::read and their links expose GoTo destinations; outline activation reads /A and scans the flattened chain for GoTo; annotation event routes perform actions through ViewState::perform_all. Catalog /OpenAction is split by shape: Destination::open_action applies a GoTo destination, while script_sites::open_action handles JavaScript chains. Generic catalog actions are not passed through the ordinary action perform route, and the viewer opening path explicitly notes that action OpenAction is not performed. Screen annotations and FDF fields listed in the paragraph are outside this tree's supported families. Existing tests exercise annotation triggers and OpenAction destinations/scripts, but do not prove generic non-GoTo OpenAction execution; this is a scope boundary for §12.6.1's broad framing, not evidence that every action type is required here. Tests read and inspected; not run in this audit.
test_result: Not run in this audit.

requirement: Next may contain one action dictionary or an array; array members are performed in array order, and each member's own Next subtree is performed before proceeding to its next sibling.
errata: No applicable EC3 correction found.
evidence: push() appends the current recognized action, then walks a dictionary or array. For array elements the loop recursively calls push before the next sibling, producing depth-first order. The cited test's root array has URI then JavaScript; the URI's Next is Launch. Its exact expected Hide, URI, Launch, JavaScript distinguishes depth-first order from breadth-first and checks the root precedes children. Fixture is a parser-local synthetic document without a page tree; this is adequate for action::read's direct dictionary walk but not a complete PDF conformance witness. The separate test draft checks occurrence preservation when an indirect reference appears twice in one array, which the current global visited-set suppresses. Parent: Table196 requires array actions in order; no text collapses two non-cyclic occurrences into one. This is an inferred consequence of that ordered sequence, not an explicit duplicate-reference sentence. Exact reader output drops the second LastPage occurrence.
test_result: FAIL after distinct-member order positive control PASS

requirement: Interactive processors are recommended to handle anomalous action graphs reasonably; in particular, a self-referential action ought not execute more than once. This is recommendation-level cycle robustness, not a producer permission to create cycles.
errata: No applicable EC3 correction found.
evidence: The global BTreeSet of visited indirect object IDs bounds cycles, and the cited two-node Hide/Launch cycle asserts exactly two outputs. This demonstrates a closing-cycle guard and termination. The current mechanism also drops a later non-cyclic occurrence of a previously visited action object in a sibling array; the normative text specifically recommends at-most-once for self-reference, while separately requiring ordered array actions. The draft regression isolates that tension. The note does not mandate this particular global deduplication policy. Tests read and inspected; not run here.
test_result: Not run in this audit.

errata: Issue #700 changes the table caption from Annex O.3 to Annex O.1; the published caption remains Annex O.3. errata-read.md:2165.
evidence: page_number accepts only unsigned decimal digits with optional leading plus, parses to u32, and rejects zero. The open arm subtracts one for the viewer's zero-based index and moves only when within page_count. The page=3 test asserts index 2. The parser test covers zero, negative, malformed, exponent and inf forms; page=12pt end-to-end asserts no movement and a named report. Out-of-range recovery is an implementation choice beyond the row's stated valid-page behavior.
test_result: The parser malformed-number and page open tests passed in model-tests-with-worker.log and interaction-tests.log, respectively.

requirement: Before URL resolution, convert relative file-spec bytes to a relative URL by percent-escaping bytes unsafe under RFC 3986 or outside 7-bit US-ASCII.

evidence: The clause says to escape bytes in a relative file specification when the filesystem is URL-based, while §7.11.5 says /FS /URL /F is already an RFC 3986 URL with its own character-encoding requirements. A draft using non-ASCII raw bytes in /FS /URL /F is nonconforming input and does not prove a defect. No route was found that opens the source PDF through a URL-based filesystem and then resolves an ordinary relative file specification. The current GoToE path handles /FS /URL, emits the URI as NeedsFile, and the host routes TargetRoot through read_import (under_remote_documents=false), which treats an absolute URL as a local path and refuses it; no URL library or network fetcher corrects or consumes the target. Keep the byte-escaping feature mapped but unresolved for this reader; do not call it an implementation gap absent a valid reachable case.

The should statements bind writer quality rather than require a reader to reject a file without either key.

evidence: Input values are clipped to Domain and pushed as `Value::Real`. The evaluator takes remaining stack items but truncates outputs to Range length, pads short results with zero, and converts Boolean outputs via `Value::number()`; thus it does not report either explicit §7.10.5.3 error. Empty-stack underflow is separately and deliberately read as integer zero; that is a documented departure and should not be redescribed as a reading of the standard. ADR 0412 §6 explicitly leaves the output-count error, answered by padding with zeroes, untouched; this is a documented deliberate departure, not an accidental unreviewed behavior. The draft has valid one-output controls and records current truncation and Boolean-conversion results. Public Function::eval returns Vec<f32> only, with no runtime error channel; these observations document the architectural limit without asserting parse-time rejection. No Cargo run was made.

requirement: The implementation provides at least 100 stack entries; overflow of its stack is an error. A writer must keep brace nesting depth at 255 or less.
source_location: Original ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.pdf printed p. 132; EC3 Markdown lines 3851–3852
errata: No EC3 change to this subclause.
evidence: CPU constant MAX_STACK is 1000, so it has at least 100 slots. Existing `an_unbounded_push_is_bounded` asserts only `values.len() <= MAX_STACK`, which reads the implementation’s own ceiling and would still pass if MAX_STACK regressed below 100. `Instruction::Push` silently declines a push at capacity; no error/report is returned, contrary to the explicit overflow error. The separate raster reference has capacity100 and a 101-entry refusal case, but it does not exercise pdf-colour’s evaluator. Drafts prove the 100-entry floor and require the current CPU implementation’s 1000-entry overflow to error; not run. The only current writer uses a fixed program with one level of conditional-brace nesting, below 255.

evidence: is_delimiter contains exactly the eight general bytes. next_token_at dispatches slash, parentheses, angle brackets, square brackets, and percent according to their syntax; doubled angle brackets are dictionary tokens. Type 4 compilation uses its own tokenizer and does not rely on this general lexer. Existing brace assertion distinguishes /A{B} as one four-byte name rather than a two-byte name plus extra tokens; the writer test asserts escaped brace spelling and readback. The existing name-escaping test also feeds each SHAPES sample through the lexer and asserts the encoded name stays one token; the new test checks all eight class memberships and both brace exclusions. This reflects Issue #365, not an unconditional reading of its ten table rows.
test_command: cargo test -p pdf-syntax --test lexical_spec_audit; cargo test -p pdf-syntax lexer::tests::a_brace_is_a_regular_character_outside_a_type_4_program; cargo test -p pdf-syntax --test name_escaping a_brace_in_a_name_is_written_as_its_hexadecimal_code_by_choice
test_result: The focused target passed all eight general delimiter-class assertions and brace/high-byte regularity assertions (4/4; `scratchpad/r1983/spec-audit/lexical-target.log`). Existing name-boundary, brace, and writer-choice tests passed in the baseline syntax suite.

requirement: Every byte other than white space or a delimiter is regular, including bytes outside ASCII. Consecutive regular characters form one token. PDF syntax is case-sensitive, so upper and lower case letters differ.
errata: No regular-character erratum found.
evidence: REGULAR is built as the complement of the white-space and delimiter predicates; read_regular_run consumes consecutive bytes from that table. The new assertion checks braces, #, 0x80, and 0xFF as regular, and asserts that A-0x80-a stays one borrowed keyword while a space separates the next token. Existing numeric-run assertions show a token does not split at a letter after its numeric prefix. The new case-sensitivity assertion uses separate uppercase/lowercase runs as regular values; the code preserves bytes verbatim.
test_command: cargo test -p pdf-syntax --test lexical_spec_audit; cargo test -p pdf-syntax lexer::tests::a_digit_run_ending_in_letters_is_one_token
test_result: The focused target passed the high-byte regular run and distinct uppercase/lowercase token assertions (4/4; `scratchpad/r1983/spec-audit/lexical-target.log`). Existing numeric regular-run tests passed in the baseline syntax suite.

requirement: Character-class grouping applies throughout the file except inside strings, streams, and comments.
errata: No scope erratum found.
evidence: String readers consume their delimited contents using string-specific rules, stream parsing uses the dictionary length/extent rather than lexing payload bytes as ordinary syntax, and comments are consumed by skip_whitespace. Existing string and stream tests exercise those separate contexts; the new comment fixture verifies delimiter-like and high-bit bytes in a comment do not escape into following tokens. A blanket every-byte token test would only prove progress, so it is not treated as evidence for this scope behavior.
test_command: cargo test -p pdf-syntax --test lexical_spec_audit; cargo test -p pdf-syntax --test spec_stream_extent_delimiter
test_result: The focused target passed the comment fixture containing delimiter-like and high-bit bytes through CR, LF, and CR-LF boundaries (4/4; `scratchpad/r1983/spec-audit/lexical-target.log`). Existing string and stream scope-interaction assertions passed in the baseline syntax suite.

requirement: Percent outside a string, and within a content stream, starts a comment extending through bytes before but not including EOL. A processor should ignore comments, and shall treat each comment as one white-space separator for lexical conversion. Other comments have no defined semantics and writers need not preserve them; %PDF-n.m and %%EOF have their §7.5 meanings.
errata: No §7.2.4 erratum found; NOTE 2 says this clause was clarified in the 2020 edition. Issue #365 was misfiled under §7.2.4 in the errata index due to page heading placement, but its subject is §7.2.3 Table 2; see doc/errata-read.md's Issue #365 finding.
evidence: skip_whitespace consumes from % up to CR or LF, leaves the marker for the whitespace branch, then continues at the following token. This makes the comment itself separate adjacent regular tokens even without a space before %. The pre-existing lexer assertion `1 % comment\n2` only shows whitespace-plus-comment and LF; the new fixture removes the space before %, includes percent and delimiter-looking bytes inside the comment, and checks CR, LF, and CR-LF endings independently. Type 4 comments have a separate reader in function.rs and its test asserts the comment ends at line boundary. Version headers and %%EOF are separately consumed by §7.5 paths; ordinary comment contents are ignored and not preserved by the writer.
test_command: cargo test -p pdf-syntax --test lexical_spec_audit comments_separate_tokens_and_stop_at_each_eol_form; cargo test -p pdf-colour a_comment_runs_to_the_end_of_its_line
test_result: The focused target passed the adjacent-token comment test for CR, LF, and CR-LF endings (4/4; `scratchpad/r1983/spec-audit/lexical-target.log`). Existing lexer and Type 4 comment tests passed in the baseline syntax suite.

requirement: Except for the PDF header and %%EOF comments governed by §7.5, this document assigns no semantics to comment contents, and writers are not required to preserve comments.
errata: No erratum found.
test_refs: crates/pdf-syntax/src/version.rs (file-level header parsing test reference; no exact function cited)
crates/pdf-syntax/tests/cross_references.rs (file-level EOF test reference; no exact function cited)
evidence: This is a scope clarification, a permission for writers, and a delegation of the two special comment meanings to §7.5. It does not require preserving ordinary comments or rejecting their contents. Reader ignores ordinary comment bytes as lexical input; §7.5 separately consumes the header and EOF markers. No standalone conformance test is required for this clarification beyond the comment-boundary behavior above.
test_result: Not applicable as an independent behavior; §7.5 owns the special comment meanings.

requirement: A supported action in a /Next chain executes at its position in the depth-first sequence, including when a JavaScript action is interleaved with an action performed by the viewer.
source_location: Effective EC3 §12.6.2 Table 196 /Next and Note 1. Table 201 §12.6.4.17 identifies JavaScript as an action type; it remains an action in this common action sequence when the reader has a runner.
errata: No direct erratum to Table 196 /Next or Note 1 found.
evidence: The standard requires the next action after its parent and recursively orders array branches. The action reader flattens supported actions depth-first, and the view-state script walker independently extracts JavaScript in depth-first order. On a public link activation, however, interact::activate first runs every script in the annotation's /A chain, then removes JavaScript refusals from the action vector, then performs the remaining actions in their flattened order. Thus script and non-script actions are not interleaved at their /Next positions. The draft uses a SetOCGState root followed by a JavaScript /Next action and observes the current layer state through ScriptEvent.document; Table 196 order requires the runner to see the layer already ON. A reverse-order positive control (JavaScript root then SetOCGState) requires the runner to see it OFF, while final Query::Layers confirms the later action takes effect. This is public-viewer state observation, not an external test log. Root execution confirms preceding SetOCGState is not reflected in the following script snapshot, although final viewer layers are ON. Reverse JS-then-action sees OFF and final ON as required. This is a selected Link consumer finding; other consumers remain code-supported only.
test_result: FAIL expected in interpolation-mixed-action-target.log, reverse-order and final-state controls PASS
parent_review: Root read Table196/Note1, ADR1602/1750/1752/1904 and actual interact::activate sequence. Corrected ScriptRunners import before compilation. Public-runner snapshot compares cross-kind order with reversed-chain positive control.

requirement: For a text field with /MaxLen, its text has a maximum length in characters; an interactive text-entry control must prevent the user from leaving a longer text value.
source_location: ISO 32000-2 §12.7.5.3, printed pp. 539–540 / physical pp. 554–555; Table 232 on printed p. 541 / physical p. 556.
errata: EC3 Issue #191, physical p. 556 / printed p. 541, filed under §12.7.5.4 but applying to §12.7.5.3/Table 232: /MaxLen is an integer value >= 0. Zero is permitted and denotes a maximum of zero characters.
evidence: Positive MaxLen is installed on GTK's ordinary Entry and Qt's QLineEdit variants. It is not applied on GTK TextView or PasswordEntry, nor on Qt QPlainTextEdit. These widgets emit their full contents through FieldChange::Set/textChanged, which the GTK/Qt host routes to Edit::SetField. Thus an ordinary typed value longer than the field's /MaxLen reaches the document on the multiline paths and GTK password path. Existing tests prove the metadata reaches ControlKind/bridge, not that the actual widgets enforce it. This is a host-entry gap; it does not establish that the model's direct ViewState::set_field API must truncate arbitrary callers. Parent ran real controls::build with GTK test-thread macro under Xvfb. Ordinary Entry accepts ab and rejects excess c (PASS). No-limit multiline/password controls accept abc; their MaxLen2 variants accept legal ab then excess c and both widget text and callback payload become abc (FAIL). MaxLen0 ordinary Entry also accepts abc (FAIL). Sequential insertion avoids requiring one particular policy for an oversized paste. Zero oracle permits no changed callback when insertion is rejected. This is a native widget/callback test, not a full OS-keyboard-to-save test.

requirement: In Unicode text strings, an escape is ESC, a two-byte BCP 47 language code, optional two-byte ISO 3166 country code, ESC; it indicates the language of subsequent text and contains no visible character.
